entry.title: Praia da Vieira, Marinha Grande
entry.summary: Praia da Vieira is a wide beach of golden sand on the central Atlantic coast of Portugal, with traditional fishing boats pulled up on the sand and the Leiria pine forest behind. The sea is strong and cool, so swimming is best in the lifeguarded area.

entry.title: Pramousquier Beach
entry.summary: Pramousquier is a quiet sandy bay between Le Lavandou and Cavaliere on the Var coast, backed by pine woods and low hills. The water is clear and calm, and the beach is much less busy than the big resorts nearby.

entry.title: Biodola Beach, Elba
entry.summary: Biodola is a wide bay of pale sand and fine gravel on the north coast of Elba, west of Portoferraio, with turquoise water and green hills on both sides. The water is shallow and clear, and a few hotels stand behind the beach.

entry.title: Playa de El Sardinero, Santander
entry.summary: El Sardinero is the main beach area of Santander in Cantabria, made up of two wide sandy bays divided by a rocky point. A seafront of elegant belle epoque buildings, gardens and the casino stands behind the sand.

entry.title: Playa del Postiguet, Alicante
entry.summary: Playa del Postiguet is the main city beach of Alicante, a curved stretch of golden sand below the Santa Barbara castle on its rock. The water is shallow and warm in summer, and a palm-lined promenade runs along the back of the beach.

entry.title: Copacabana Beach, Dubrovnik
entry.summary: Copacabana is a long pebble beach on the Babin Kuk peninsula in Dubrovnik, with clear water and a lively beach scene. Beach bars, water sports and hotels sit behind it, and the old town is a short bus ride away.

entry.title: Livadi Beach, Astypalaia
entry.summary: Livadi is the main beach of Astypalaia, a green valley bay with pebbles and sand below the whitewashed Chora and its Venetian castle. Tamarisk trees give shade, and a few tavernas sit just behind the beach.

entry.title: Agia Marina Beach, Aegina
entry.summary: Agia Marina is a lively resort village on the east coast of Aegina, with a sandy beach and very shallow water that suits families. Ferries from Piraeus reach the island in about an hour, so it works well as a day trip from Athens.

entry.title: Platja de Sa Riera, Begur
entry.summary: Sa Riera is a quiet cove below the village of Begur on the Costa Brava, with a small beach of coarse sand, clear water and pine-covered headlands. Old fishermen boat houses stand at one end, and the water is calm and sheltered.

entry.title: Suha Punta Beach, Rab
entry.summary: Suha Punta is a pine-covered peninsula on the island of Rab, with rocky and pebbly coves, flat stone platforms and clear water. A footpath runs along the shore, and the pines give shade for most of the day.

entry.title: Pupnatska Luka Beach, Korcula
entry.summary: Pupnatska Luka is a long pebble bay on the south coast of Korcula, below the village of Pupnat, with clear turquoise water and forested hills on both sides. It is one of the best-known beaches and stays quiet outside the peak weeks.

entry.title: Praia do Furadouro
entry.summary: Praia do Furadouro is a long, wide beach of golden sand in Ovar, Aveiro district, known for its traditional painted fishing boats on the sand. A seafront promenade runs behind the beach, and the sea is strong and often rough.

entry.title: Praia de Mira
entry.summary: Praia de Mira is a wide, gently sloping beach of fine sand on the central Atlantic coast of Portugal, with dunes behind and the Barrinha de Mira lagoon close by. The sea can be cool and strong, and the beach is large enough to stay uncrowded.

entry.title: Kalogria Beach
entry.summary: Kalogria is a very long beach of fine sand in the western Peloponnese, near Patras, backed by the Strofylia pine forest and coastal wetlands. The sea shelves gently and the dunes are wild, so the beach feels open and uncrowded.

entry.title: Cala Bianca, Marina di Camerota
entry.summary: Cala Bianca is a small cove of white pebbles and clear green water on the Cilento coast, south of Marina di Camerota, with an old watchtower on the rocks above. Most visitors arrive by boat from the harbour, and the coast is part of the Cilento national park.

entry.title: Baia di Sistiana
entry.summary: Baia di Sistiana is a sheltered bay in the Gulf of Trieste, below white limestone cliffs on the Karst coast. Swimmers use pebble beaches and rocky platforms with deep, clear water, and a marina sits at the head of the bay.

entry.title: Playa d en Bossa, Ibiza
entry.summary: Playa d en Bossa is the longest beach on Ibiza, a wide stretch of fine sand south of Ibiza Town with shallow water. It is the busiest and most lively beach, with beach clubs, bars and hotels along the seafront.

entry.title: Playa de Ondarreta
entry.summary: Ondarreta is the quieter of the two city beaches of San Sebastian, set at the western end of the bay below Monte Igueldo. The sand is fine and golden, and a line of tamarisk trees and a long promenade run behind it.

entry.title: Capo di Feno Beach
entry.summary: Capo di Feno is a long sandy beach on the wild coast west of Ajaccio in Corsica. Open to the Atlantic-facing swell and the wind, it is popular with surfers, and the maquis-covered hills behind keep it feeling remote.

entry.title: Arone Beach, Piana
entry.summary: Arone is a long beach of pale sand at the southern end of the Gulf of Porto in western Corsica, close to the Calanques de Piana. The water is turquoise, the sea floor shelves gently, and wild hills rise behind the beach.

entry.title: Escalet Beach, Ramatuelle
entry.summary: The Escalet is a small cove near Cap Camarat on the Ramatuelle peninsula, reached through vineyards and pine woods. The sand is coarse and golden, the water is clear, and rocky points close the bay on both sides.

entry.title: Bijeca Beach, Medulin
entry.summary: Bijeca is a gently sloping beach of sand and fine pebbles on the Medulin bay in southern Istria, shaded by pine trees. The water stays shallow for a long way out, which suits families with small children.

entry.title: Raduca Beach, Primosten
entry.summary: Raduca is a long pebble beach south of Primosten in central Dalmatia, backed by pines and olive trees. The water is clear, and small islets sit on the horizon, which makes the sunsets especially good.

entry.title: Kolovare Beach, Zadar
entry.summary: Kolovare is the main city beach of Zadar, on the eastern side of the old town peninsula. The beach is made of sand and fine pebbles, the water is shallow and clear, and pines give some shade behind the sand.

entry.title: Praia da Gale, Albufeira
entry.summary: Praia da Gale is a long beach of golden sand in the Algarve, west of Albufeira, backed by low sandy cliffs and with calm water. It is a popular family beach with restaurants behind and a walkway along the shore.

entry.title: Praia de Moledo
entry.summary: Praia de Moledo is a long beach of fine sand in the north of Portugal, near Caminha, with pine woods behind and the Minho river and the Spanish coast in view. The Atlantic water is cool, and the beach is popular with families and surfers.

entry.title: Praia da Amoreira, Aljezur
entry.summary: Praia da Amoreira is a wide beach on the Costa Vicentina near Aljezur, where a river and a lagoon meet the Atlantic below low cliffs. At low tide the sand opens up into a long shore, and the waves attract surfers and bodyboarders.

entry.title: Praia do Rostro, Fisterra
entry.summary: Praia do Rostro is a long beach of fine pale sand on the Costa da Morte in Galicia, near Fisterra and Cee, with a small lagoon behind and mountains on each side. The Atlantic waves are strong and the water is cool.

entry.title: Playa de Xago
entry.summary: Playa de Xago is a wide beach of golden sand in Asturias, near Cabo Penas, with dunes behind and strong Atlantic waves that attract surfers. The beach sits on a coast of cliffs and green headlands.

entry.title: Playazo de Rodalquilar
entry.summary: El Playazo is a long beach of sand and fine gravel near Rodalquilar, in the Cabo de Gata-Nijar natural park in Almeria, with the ruined Castillo de San Ramon at the north end. Hills of red and brown volcanic rock rise behind the shore.
